title: CDNs and static files
summary: Use a content delivery network to bring public files closer to readers. Plan cache headers, versioned names, and safe rules for private responses.
introduction: Imagine each town library keeps a copy of the same public poster. Visitors can read the nearest copy. A content delivery network uses a similar idea for files such as pictures, styles, and public web pages.
learningObjectives: Explain the job of an origin and a CDN edge
Trace a public file on a cache miss and a cache hit
Use versioned file names without exposing private data

blocks.text: A **content delivery network**, or **CDN**, has servers in several locations. An **edge** is a server near some readers. The **origin** is the place the CDN asks for a file when it needs a copy.
**Static files** are saved files sent as they are, such as a book-cover picture or a style sheet. They are good CDN candidates when the same public content can be shared by many readers.

The browser also has a cache. Cache headers tell browsers and shared caches how an answer may be reused. Public caching is a choice for suitable content; it must not happen accidentally to a learner's private page.

items: The site links to a public cover named moon-cover-v1.webp.
The first reader's nearest edge has no copy. It fetches the file from the origin and keeps a copy according to the cache rules.
The next matching request can use the edge copy while it is fresh.
For a new cover, publish moon-cover-v2.webp and update the page link. Keep the old file for pages that still link to it.

blocks.code:
PUBLIC COVER
Path: /covers/moon-cover-v1.webp
Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400
First request: edge miss -> origin -> edge -> reader
Later fresh request: edge hit -> reader

UPDATED COVER
Path: /covers/moon-cover-v2.webp
Update the page to use the new path.

PRIVATE BORROWING HISTORY
Cache-Control: private, no-store
Never place the response in a shared public cache.
blocks.title: CDNs and static files plan

blocks.text: 86,400 seconds is one day. This example allows a fresh public cover to be reused for that time. It is a sample policy, not a rule for every file.
A versioned name gives changed bytes a new address. The page that points to the new address also needs a freshness rule. An old cached page can still point to the old file.

rows: Often reduces travel and origin work
The first miss may still need the origin
Old links must keep working during a rollout
Helps readers discover new file links sooner
Adds more refresh work than a long cache

blocks.text: If the origin fails, a fresh edge copy may still be served. Missing or expired files need explicit failure or stale-serving rules. A CDN is not a promise that every page works during every outage.
A cache key decides which requests share an answer. Consider the path, query, language, and any allowed variation. Do not share a private response by mistake because its key forgot who may see it.

items: A cover changes again. Pick its next versioned name and name one other thing to update.
Use moon-cover-v3.webp and update the page link. Keep older files while old pages may still request them.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not cache private borrowing history as a public answer. A fast leak is still a leak; access rules and cache rules must agree.
